title: Uses Cleanup Preview (compiler-verified, this unit)
summary: The removals a Uses Audit suggests, but verified by actually compiling
intro: Read this before applying a Uses Audit: it previews the same removals but verifies them by compiling, so a unit that is still needed is not stripped by mistake.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Uses Cleanup Preview (compiler-verified)...
steps: Open the unit in the editor
Choose drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Uses Cleanup Preview (compiler-verified)...
Review each candidate (verified by compiling) before applying

surfaces.usage: drag-lint uses-fix <unit.pas> --project <dproj> --db <file.sqlite> [--platform win32|win64] [--apply] [--remove-unused] [--only <unit,...>] [--format json|text] (compiler-verified uses cleanup; --format json lists every candidate with a status -- verified | skipped | deselected -- and --only restricts which are compiled and written, so a reviewed partial apply is expressible; a unit --only names that is in the uses clause but in no project index -- an RTL/VCL/library unit -- is decided by compiling too: removed when it has no initialization section (with --remove-unused), else moved to the implementation section, else skipped)

questions.ask: Can I remove these unused units safely?
How do I write the verified removals?
